claims.text: Funds are available for the preservation, conservation, and repair of listed historic buildings, structures, and architectural features.
Special consideration is given to projects that offer sustainable solutions for conservation and re-use, particularly for buildings at risk and of outstanding importance.
Funding can cover project costs, staff costs, fees, internships, initial exploratory work, and capital costs.
Grant sizes are generally between £1,000 and £30,000, with an average of approximately £15,000.
Larger sums may be considered in some cases.
Applications can be submitted at any time.
Stage one applications are considered on a rolling basis.
Stage two applications for over £5,000 are considered quarterly at Board meetings.
The cut-off dates for Stage two applications over £5,000 in 2026 are January 9, April 10, July 31, and October 2.
Grants of £5,000 or less are considered on a rolling basis, with a response expected within 4 weeks of submitting a Stage two application.
If successful, grantees are normally expected to claim their grant within a year and complete the project within two years.

claims.text: Funds are available for the conservation of historic interiors in places of worship that are open for regular worship.
Funds are available for the conservation of historic objects in places of worship that are open for regular worship.

Eligible historic objects include bells, books and manuscripts, clocks, decorative plasterwork, metalwork and church plate, monuments, organs, paintings, stained glass, textiles, timberwork, and wall paintings.
Funds are available for the conservation of historic structures in churchyards.
Funds are available for commissioning conservation reports.
Anglican churches must apply via the ChurchCare conservation grants scheme.
All other denominations, faiths, and cathedrals may apply directly to The Pilgrim Trust.
Applicants must take an eligibility quiz before accessing application forms.
All applications must be submitted through an online grants system called Flexigrant.
Stage 1 of the application involves submitting key project details for suitability checks, with a response expected within four weeks.
Stage 2 of the application involves setting out the application in full, and can be submitted within 12 months of a successful Stage 1 application.
Applications for £5,000 or less should receive a response within 4 weeks.
For applications over £5,000, final decisions are made by Trustees at quarterly meetings in March, June, September, and November.
The cut-off dates for applications in 2026 are January 9, April 10, July 31, and October 2.
